items.title: Lawrence Duhé Interview, 1957-06-09
items.q: when you had two clarinets in the band, you and Sidney

ctx.x: Some really, about 23, I think. Yeah. Oh, I was going to ask, I always wondered, you know, I mentioned to Mr. Bro the other day, too, when I was talking to him about when you had two clarinets in the band, you and Sidney, you played the lead, or did one play the lead?

Always played the lead, and Sidney was the hot man. He was the hot man. Always the hot man. Always was Peter. And you played more of the straight melody. Straight to let them know what's coming on, because he never could read, see, at that time. Yeah. But the minute you played it once over, that's all he tells you, let me have it. A whole lot of it he takes, too, I'm talking about. Oh, he's a great clarinetist. Oh, yeah.
Well, he's the best in the business for second, man. I'm telling you.

items.title: Lawrence Duhé Interview, 1957-06-09
items.q: No. The captain. I didn't go with Sydney a Vene, but Sydney a Vene left me was playing with me at the Hunt.

ctx.x: Gee, I never knew they had music. You all played on the JS Sydney a while too, didn't you?
No. The captain. I didn't go with Sydney a Vene, but Sydney a Vene left me was playing with me at the Hunt.
No, I mean, they both leave that Canal Street going to Resilient.
